hypothesis: Treating only EACCES and EPERM directory reads as explicit artifact exclusions will keep progress-review evidence honest without allowing one inaccessible run descendant to abort the review or its redrive.

metricsCompared.name: redriven collections aborted by an unreadable artifact directory
metricsCompared.baseline: The cited progress-review dispatch terminated with EACCES and remained an open workflow-dispatch dead letter.
metricsCompared.candidate: 0 of 1 WorkflowRuntime redrives aborted; the replacement run succeeded, the original item transitioned from open to redriven, the durable queue ended with zero open successor items, and two accessible sibling artifacts remained citeable.

metricsCompared.name: unreadable descendants represented in review evidence
metricsCompared.baseline: The inaccessible directory produced no exclusion because traversal threw before the evidence packet completed.
metricsCompared.candidate: 1 of 1 inaccessible directories was recorded by run-relative path and errno code in excluded evidence.

metricsCompared.name: focused progress-reviewer workflow regressions
metricsCompared.baseline: The suite had no unreadable-descendant redrive case.
metricsCompared.candidate: 38 of 38 progress-reviewer workflow tests passed, including the new redrive regression; TypeScript and strict-type policy checks also passed.

rationale: The candidate is narrowly fail-soft at the filesystem evidence boundary: it catches only permission-denied directory reads, records each omission, preserves deterministic traversal and artifact limits, and rethrows unexpected errors. A production-shaped WorkflowRuntime regression persists the initial EACCES dead letter, redrives its stored trigger, proves the replacement run succeeds with accessible evidence, and verifies that no successor dead letter is created.
